translation: The most important thing that happened to me the winter of 1993 was that my father returned, just a week before my mother's wedding.
One afternoon in December, he came to the school to see me.
I ran all the way to the front gate, and from afar through the iron railing, I could see him standing outside smoking.
Wearing a long black trench coat, the turned-up collar masking half of his face.
I don't know why, but even though I didn't get a clear look at him, I felt like he was having a hard time.
My heart ached, and tears welled up in my eyes.
I never thought that my mother would consider remarrying.
Perhaps subconsciously, I felt that she should continue to suffer because of my father's departure, just like me.
Moreover, I think she lacks the ability to find happiness.
Perhaps this is the case, but happiness has the ability to find her.
Isn't that so?
As a beauty, she doesn't need to work that hard.
She doesn't need to do anything, just stand in place would be enough.
I still remember, the winter of that year was particularly long, half way through April and the spring blossoms had yet to bloom.
The divorce of your parents has left you feeling very depressed.
We haven't had any new games in a while, and when the evening comes we would just aimlessly sit on the roof of the tower of the dead.
Among the body parts scattered around the yard, there were now a few more arms.
We used hooks to pull them together, forming a thousand-hand Guanyin.
Actually, my father had no clue about doing business; he just went to join a distant cousin with whom he was not very familiar.
My grandmother had a younger sister who moved to Beijing in her early years, where she later got married and had children.
This cousin was the eldest son of his family and had always been regarded as an outsider within the whole clan.
Just now you said that everyone has a time when their luck begins, as if life suddenly has reins on it.
I think it was when I was eight.
That autumn, my father left Jinan and went to Beijing alone.
Ever since then, I have no longer had a home.
I have no intention of keeping the appointment.
Regardless of the reason, I don't think it's necessary for us to meet again.
I sat on the sofa, smoking one cigarette after another.
As the sky gradually darkened, a sudden knock resounded at the door.
Send
The boy carrying water buckets stood at the doorway, saying he was off to deliver water to a family in the western suburbs.
He wore a dirty, gray woolen hat, with a vacant look on his face.
Our conversation was very difficult.
Every time I fell silent, I felt a pressure on my heart, and all I wanted was to end the meeting quickly.
You seem to have noticed something, but you're still trying hard to find a topic.
The tea cooled off, the white mist in the room had completely dissipated, and you finally rose to take your leave.
I had just closed the door and let out a sigh of relief when the doorbell rang again.
You stood at the doorway, asking me to come to the small white building later.
Before I could even decline, you had already left the building.
I walked to the kitchen and turned off the stove.
Half of the water had evaporated from the kettle, and the whole room was shrouded in white mist.
You sit down uncomfortably, watching me pour tea.
"Do you still live with your grandmother and aunt?"
You ask.
I'm telling you, my grandmother has passed away.
Now I live with my aunt.
"She never settled down," you ask.
"Hmm.

The white breath you exhale, the curly hair stirred up by the wind, the slight tremble of your knees under your coat hemall these convince me that your presence is real and not just a continuation of a previous dream.
It's been eighteen years, so it wouldn't be strange if you didn't recognize me.
You're not wearing any makeup, your pale face is a little swollen, but at least you did not disappoint everyone's expectations, you have grown into a beauty.
Only, her small peach-heart shaped face was dark and gloomy, she had the demeanor of having been in the big city for a long time.
You ask me if you look different from what I imagined.
I gave a noncommittal smile.
To be honest, I've never imagined what you would look like grown up.
As far as I'm concerned, everything about you has been put into a file and sealed with wax.
It might hurt to say this, but honestly, I did not look forward to seeing you again.
I open my eyes.
You are standing at the doorway.
I have no idea how long you've been standing there.
You might have even seen me laughing in my dream.
There's the sorrow of waking up, in its most vulnerable state.
Cheng Gong, you whispered my name in a very hoarse voice, as if you haven't spoken for a long time.
It's about to snow, the sky is heavily overcast, and the house is pitch dark.
The water on the stove was boiling, gurgling and rolling.
I looked at you carefully for a moment, certain that I did not recognize you.
But in the dim light, I suddenly felt that this stranger standing opposite me seemed to have a deep connection with my life.
That kind of feeling sends chills down one's spine.
I tried hard to recall, the cards of memory flipping through my mind.
And then you said, "You are Li Jiaqi.
